units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
He looks anxiously at his wife .
Eagerly .
Oh yes, Robert, you should do that. It is your duty to do that.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: It is much to surrender.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: No; it will be much to gain.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN walks up and down the room with a troubled expression .
Then comes over to his wife , and puts his hand on her shoulder .
And you would be happy living somewhere alone with me, abroad perhaps, or in the country away from London, away from public life? You would have no regrets?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Oh! none, Robert.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Sadly .
And your ambition for me? You used to be ambitious for me.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Oh, my ambition! I have none now, but that we two may love each other. It was your ambition that led you astray. Let us not talk about ambition.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: LORD GORING returns from the conservatory , looking very pleased with himself , and with an entirely new buttonhole that some one has made for him .
Going towards him .
Arthur, I have to thank you for what you have done for me. I don’t know how I can repay you.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Shakes hands with him .
My dear fellow, I’ll tell you at once. At the present moment, under the usual palm tree . . . I mean in the conservatory . . .
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Enter MASON.
Lord Caversham.
units.name: MASON

units.text: That admirable father of mine really makes a habit of turning up at the wrong moment. It is very heartless of him, very heartless indeed.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Enter LORD CAVERSHAM.
MASON goes out .
Good morning, Lady Chiltern! Warmest congratulations to you, Chiltern, on your brilliant speech last night. I have just left the Prime Minister, and you are to have the vacant seat in the Cabinet.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: With a look of joy and triumph .
A seat in the Cabinet?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Yes; here is the Prime Minister’s letter.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Hands letter .
Takes letter and reads it .
A seat in the Cabinet!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Certainly, and you well deserve it too. You have got what we want so much in political life nowadays—high character, high moral tone, high principles.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: To LORD GORING.
Everything that you have not got, sir, and never will have.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I don’t like principles, father. I prefer prejudices.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN is on the brink of accepting the Prime Minister’s offer , when he sees wife looking at him with her clear , candid eyes .
He then realises that it is impossible .
I cannot accept this offer, Lord Caversham. I have made up my mind to decline it.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Decline it, sir!
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: My intention is to retire at once from public life.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Angrily .
Decline a seat in the Cabinet, and retire from public life? Never heard such damned nonsense in the whole course of my existence. I beg your pardon, Lady Chiltern. Chiltern, I beg your pardon.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: To LORD GORING.
Don’t grin like that, sir.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: No, father.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Lady Chiltern, you are a sensible woman, the most sensible woman in London, the most sensible woman I know. Will you kindly prevent your husband from making such a . . . from taking such . . . Will you kindly do that, Lady Chiltern?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I think my husband is right in his determination, Lord Caversham. I approve of it.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: You approve of it? Good heavens!
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Taking her husband’s hand .
I admire him for it. I admire him immensely for it. I have never admired him so much before. He is finer than even I thought him.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN
